PATROL, in war, a round or march made by the
guards or watch in the night time, to obferve what
paffes in the ftreets, and to fecure the peace and tranquil¬
lity of a city or camp. The patrol generally confilts of

They go every hour of the night, from the beating

fembling together : they are to fee the lights in the fol-
diers barracks put out, and to take up all the foldiers
they find out of their quarters. Sometimes patrols con-
fift of an officer and 30 or 40 men, as well infantry as

PETAL ISM, a mode of deciding on the guilt of ci- , Petau'
tizens, fimilar to the Athenian Ostracism. It was intro¬

PINEA, or PiGNE, in commerce, is a term ufed in

Each piece or cuerpo is again kneaded up with fea-

forward it; and, in fume mines, they are obliged to
ufe fire. To try whether or no the mixture and a-
